#202 - Shield Money

Chapter 196 Shield Money

The inheritance system in any region is an important tool for maintaining social stability. For example, the eldest son inherits political identity and sacrificial rights, and the other sons share property with the eldest son.

Obviously, this kind of institutional system will make the family strength weaken a lot during the transition period, or even collapse, thereby strengthening the authority of the government, the emperor, etc.

Since the ancient times, the lords of Westeros have tried their best to avoid the situation where the second son or youngest son comes to divide the family assets and territory and is taken advantage of by rival families. Therefore, one heir usually gets all the family resources.

When the Andals came across the Narrow Sea with their faith in the Seven Stars and iron weapons in hand, the Andal inheritance method in which the eldest son takes all began to become popular in Westeros. Quite a few families of the ancestors were affected by this. The eldest daughter's succession order began to be lowered.

The Dorne region joined by the Rhoynar was not affected by this, and they still retained the indiscriminate inheritance method between the eldest daughter and the eldest son.

But no matter in Dorne, the five central countries, or in the north, the second sons cannot get family resources. After the birth of the eldest brother's child, they lose their status as backup heirs and are kicked out of the house to survive alone. .

Of course, the second sons of the great nobles do not have to be so embarrassed. Their families can provide positions to the second sons who have received aristocratic military training so that they can continue to serve the family. However, Westeros only has six hundred non-repeated noble surnames. There are only fifty or sixty big noble families, and the remaining second sons of the family can only go out to work as wandering knights or mercenaries.

A slightly wealthier and more generous family could give their second sons a suit of iron armor and even a war horse, while a less wealthy or more iron-blooded family would simply kick them out without even decent clothes.

Jules Bracken is a less standard example, because his martial arts are not worthy of his status as an armed nobleman, but his rich wandering experience is worthy of any second son.

The nobles were like this, but the second sons of wealthy knight families were even more cruel. They were born to fight for the superior lords.

But fortunately, the second son of a wealthy knight would not threaten the inheritance rights of the eldest son, so he usually did not need to travel too far from his place of birth and could just find a position in the escort team of a nearby lord.

For example, Sandor Clegane, the hound, joined the Lannister family's army after his brother The Mountain inherited the family fortune. He achieved great success at the age of fourteen in the Usurper's War, and was therefore recognized by Tywin. The Duke was sent as Cersei's bodyguard, and was later assigned by Cersei to her eldest son, Prince Joffrey, as her personal bodyguard.

"The second sons, youngest sons, and illegitimate sons of small families and wealthy knights often have good military training, but because they conflict with the eldest son's inheritance rights, they are kicked out of the family and go to the Eastern Continent to work as mercenaries. They spend their entire lives away from their hometown and relatives, and live in a different country. As a king, I cannot stand this cold-blooded tradition."

Arthur first expressed his regret for his second son and illegitimate son wandering around, and then changed the subject and emphasized that incorporating the second sons into the royal standing army was a mutually beneficial situation.

"So the second sons and illegitimate sons of nobles over the age of fifteen must come to King's Landing to join the royal standing army in accordance with the Kingdom's laws. The Iron Throne will generously give them salary and officer positions, as well as the opportunity to advance to the territory based on military merit. "

"Of course, some second sons are still the heirs of their older brothers. The royal army will consider this situation and provide these people with easier civilian or logistical positions."

"This bill will be implemented from next month, which is the first month of the 300th year of Aegon's conquest. Let's name it the 300 Years Second Son Act!"

Arthur explained the details of the second son's bill one by one, and the expressions of the courtiers also changed accordingly. The most obvious change was that of the little devil.

The new Duke of Lannister is obviously wise enough. The king's move will definitely attract a large number of outstanding warriors who have received military training since childhood but were lower in the order of succession.

The strengthening of the king's power meant the reduction of the lord's power.

Lord Redwyne, who has just put on the badge of the Queen, does not have Tyrion's wisdom. He only cares about one thing:

"Your Majesty, does my son Hopper also need to abide by this law?"

Whether or not his son will stay in King's Landing is secondary. What Paxter is concerned about is that because of this bill, his younger son Hobb has lost some of his freedom.

For example, you cannot control where you want to go.

Prince Oberyn, Tyrion and others sitting on one side of the round table looked at the king with their necks crooked, wondering how far this bill would be implemented.

In order to win the support of the Redwynes, Hobble might not be bound by this, Tyrion thought to himself.

But Tyrion was disappointed.

The king declared unequivocally: "As Hand of the King and Prime Minister of the Royal Council, Lord Paxter must take the lead in setting an example. Your second son, Hob Redwine, must join the royal standing army."

Earl Paxter's face was uncertain, and he couldn't tell whether this was good or bad.

Arthur noticed this and gave him some comfort: "But don't worry, as a member of the top nobility, Hobo will naturally not be as strictly required as members of small families. He only needs to express his stance to join, and the follow-up will be as follows: In the name of protecting his cousin Queen Margaery, Sir Hopper is stationed at the Red Keep."

After hearing this arrangement, Paxter finally felt relieved.

"You are such a wise king!" After his own interests are protected, Earl Redwin will never be stingy with his compliments.

He has established his eldest son, the terrifying Sir Horace, as his heir, and Hopper's mission is to consolidate the family's various rights and interests.

As the queen's cousin, Hobo is the most suitable choice to stay in the Red Keep. Firstly, he can consolidate his relationship with the Tyrell family. Secondly, he can become familiar with the royal family and lay the foundation for his smooth entry into the Royal Council when he is older. .

Tyrion raised the inseparable wine glass in his hand and casually echoed: "Cheers to the wise Arthur I!"

The king glanced sideways at him, sensing that the Lannister lord was more interested in drinking than flattering.

The matter of the Second Son Act came to an end, and War Minister Aenys took the lead in talking about the war in the Stormlands.

"Your Majesty, Count Matus' advance is a little slow. His military camp has only reached the edge of the territory directly under Storm's End, and there is no sign of going south to siege the castle. The big families in the northern part of the Stormlands, such as Hay Hall, Tongmen City, Fort Felwood and other places also did not send soldiers to participate in the battle. "

Countess Sheila Errol of Hay Hall, Lord Heywood Fell of Felwood Castle (also translated as Woodfall City), Ralph Buckler, Earl of Bronzegate City, and others, as well as the Lord of Dusk Advent Hall, Dusk The star, Selwyn Tarth, basically sided with Renly first and then turned to Stannis.

After the death of Stannis, these people returned to the Iron Throne, that is, Arthur I, who has "orthodox" Targaryen blood. The northern families of the Stormlands basically swore an oath before and after the wedding of the king and Queen Margaery, but It seems that they are not very supportive of going south to attack the Golden Company.

The more severe Lord Randyll Tarly expressed his opinion, "Your Majesty, I suggest that you directly send an envoy from the Iron Throne to sternly warn these families that if they do not send troops south, after we have eliminated the Golden Company, we will lead our troops to They charge shield money."

Arthur pondered that the shield money in Landao's mouth was slightly different from the "shield money" in England in his previous life.

The shield money in Count Tully's mouth was the protection fee collected by the Iron Throne. According to the oath sworn by the lower-level lord when he was loyal to the upper-level lord, the main military interaction between the two sides was that when the upper-level lord was summoned, the lower-level lord had to lead the army to fight; when the lower-level lord was in trouble, The superior lord has to step in to solve the problem or lead troops to help.

The ancient British shield money was used to exempt the king from the forty-day military service, allowing knights who were unable to participate in the war to spend money to exempt themselves from the length of service.

This reminded Arthur that in the future, if the second son of a wealthy family does not want to join the royal standing army, he can use money to reduce the cost of service.

It is also a way to increase income.

"A reasonable proposal. These families must either send troops or provide food. Anyway, it cannot be the same as now." Arthur looked around and asked, "Do you have any suitable candidates to go to the northern part of the Stormlands?"

Tristan Legge, the commander of the garrison who was basically silent, cleared his throat and then suggested: "Your Majesty, Queen Sansa's bodyguard, Brienne of Tarth is the most suitable choice. She is the only one in the Evening Star." My child, the Tarth family’s influence in the Stormlands is not low.”

The successive governors of the Tars family are called Evening Stars.

Tyrion also agreed with this proposal, "Yes, Your Majesty. As far as I know, Selwyn and Brienne themselves have Targaryen blood, so they are perfect representatives of the Iron Throne."

Marquis Aenys Frey, who didn't read much, was obviously a little surprised. He widened his brown eyes and asked, "When did the Tarth family also have true dragon blood?"

This is also the doubt of the other semi-illiterate nobles.

Prince Oberyn, the only educated person on the royal council, answered this question, "During the time of Aegon V, there was a Targaryen princess who married into the Tarth family in the Hall of Evening. I remember that this princess was Aegon V. Daughter of Daena Targaryen."

Danila was once engaged to Aegon V, but after Aegon V traveled half of the Seven Kingdoms with the legendary knight Duncan the Tall, he fell in love freely with Bess Blackwood, so Danila married an unknown person. character (most likely Tall Duncan).

The Red Viper himself has Targaryen blood and has read a lot of books, so he can say something about these twists and turns of relatives.

The king was also surprised by this remote and unpopular blood relationship, "That's Brienne. When she succeeds in getting the Stormland family to provide food and troops, I will specially order to have a knight with a very good reputation seal her. For a true knight."

Arthur himself was not a knight, so he could not make others knights. Even if he was forcibly made a knight, other knights would not recognize it.

The royal meeting continued. Regarding the fact that Matus sent someone to remind Landao that there might be a problem, the king has not yet decided how to deal with it, but before he leads his army south, he will definitely find excuses to eliminate all unstable factors.

…

The Reach, Oldtown.

Even though it has been many months into late autumn, the green land is still full of harvest scenes, especially in the bustling old town.

As the sun rises, the morning fog begins to disperse, and Westeros' second largest city and largest port begins to glow with vitality.

Farmers drove oxcarts to transport crops that were redundant and could not be stored for a long time to the city in exchange for a few spare coins. Vendors carried burdens and hawked along the mead river that passed through the old town. Monks and bachelors held their heads high. Apprentices walk through the crowd from time to time, heading to the Starry Cathedral or the Academy from the courtyard or tavern. Wealthy merchants and sailors from major trading ports carry their wallets in the streets and alleys looking for the services they want.

The long winter is coming, but Old Town is like a knight taking off his armor, showing off his impressive achievements in the long summer to anyone who comes here.

The war has been going on for almost a year, but this place has not been affected much. The only thing that can show the war factor is the big iron chain across the mouth of the Mead River.

The iron chain across the river is one of the main means for Westeros to deal with the enemy's attack from the sea. King's Landing, hundreds of miles away, has also built a capstan tower to facilitate locking the Blackwater River when necessary.

Pate, with freckles on his face, looked coldly at the iron chain across the river shining with metallic luster in the early morning sun and the towering tower standing at the mouth of the Mead River, and then staggered towards the Citadel with the remaining power of apple cider.

In the past night, he and several apprentices he knew drank wine in the "Quill Pen Wine Bottle" on the island in the Mead River in the second half of the night.

He went to this tavern that has existed for 600 years to fulfill an appointment with an alchemist to exchange a key of old Dr. Wargrave for a gold dragon.

"Exchange black iron for gold dragons, exchange black iron for gold dragons..." The parrot's voice sounded, and when it reached the guilty ears of Pate, it automatically turned into this sentence.

His purpose for wanting gold dragons was also very simple. As long as he had one gold dragon, he could get the virginity of Rosie, the youngest maid of "Quill Pen Wine Barrel".

That was Rosie, Rosie who could let him play with her tender feet.

Pate fantasized about the beautiful life of eloping with Rosie in the future, "A donkey can carry both of us."

But he didn't notice that he bumped into someone.

"Good morning, Pate!" The person who was bumped took the initiative to greet him.

Pate, who was sorting the mud on his only robe, looked up and saw a tall figure wearing a brown hooded cloak.

Although the sunlight in front of him made it difficult for him to see the man's face, his voice allowed him to recognize that this was the "alchemist".

"You broke your promise!" Pate was a little angry, but he didn't dare to show his anger in his tone.

After all, he still needed this gold dragon very much.

"I got there early, but I didn't disturb you when I saw you and your companions."

The former "Jaquin", now an alchemist, stared at Pate with a casual but firm look, and without waiting for the apprentice to speak, he turned and walked towards the deep alley on the side.

Pate, who was anxious to use the gold dragon, had no choice but to follow.

If he missed this time, he would never have any chance to get a real gold dragon again, and Rosie's flowering period was approaching, and another apprentice that Pate hated, Leo Tyrell, also claimed to take Rosie's virginity.

The two walked into the deepest part of the alley, one after the other.

"The key is here, where is the gold dragon?"

Pate, who was still anxious for the gold dragon, couldn't hold his breath and broke the silence between the two first.

The alchemist with his hood off reached into the purse at his waist, took out the largest coin, and threw it to the apprentice who was watching eagerly.

Pate caught the gold coin that had drawn a perfect curve, "This is not theft, this is just an exchange, exchanging black iron for gold."

He comforted himself with a poor excuse, and then began to identify the authenticity of the gold dragon coin.

Like all the gold dragon coins in Westeros, this gold coin also has a three-headed dragon emblem on one side and a tall and handsome Targaryen king's upper body on the other side.

Among the existing gold dragon coins, the most are the ones with the upper body pattern of Jaehaerys I, who had the longest reign, and the others are much less.

Although Pate has seen the portraits of the Targaryen kings, he couldn't figure out whose upper body portrait was printed on the gold dragon coin in his hand.

Of course, Pate didn't know that the owner of this portrait, Daemon Blackfyre I, had never ascended the Iron Throne.

The one in his hand was the commemorative currency issued by the Golden Group on the continent of Essos.

Feeling the alchemist staring at him again, in order to pretend to be experienced, Pate had to learn how others identified the gold coin, put it in his mouth, and bit it hard with his big teeth.

When he took out the gold coin, there was indeed a bite mark.

"Real gold coin!" After getting the gold dragon, Pate suddenly hesitated, "Are you going to steal the book?"

The key of old Dr. Wargrave can open a cellar, which is locked with some of the only Valyrian scrolls in the world.

"It's none of your business!" The alchemist said coldly.

After getting the gold dragon coin, Pate only wanted to play with Rosie, "Oh, then it's a deal!"

He handed the stolen key to the man and turned away.

But the cobblestone road under his feet suddenly floated up, "What's going on, I don't understand."

"You will never understand." Someone replied.

After a few breaths, Pate fell in the alley, and then the alchemist walked over quickly, changed his hooded cloak to Pate, and then began to peel off the face of this poor apprentice.

Before the morning fog completely dispersed, the new Pate reappeared on the streets of the old town. He imitated the shaking movements of Pate after drinking cider and slowly moved towards the huge building complex of the Citadel.

Having been investigating the Citadel for two months, the "new Pate" was much more familiar with this place than the previous owner of this face. He entered the residence of old Dr. Wargrave with ease.

The old doctor was elected as the mayor of the Citadel this year, but because of his old age, a middle-aged doctor named Theobold was appointed as the mayor.

The new Pate quietly approached the door of the old doctor's bedroom and listened to the conversation inside.

"Yes, Marwin is untrustworthy. His mind is full of magic, which is completely contrary to the concept of our Citadel." A low voice said.

"I also support Dr. Ryan. He is a firm non-magic faction. It is most appropriate for him to go to King's Landing."

The second panting voice was obviously from Old Wargrave.

After the people in the bedroom finished their conversation, the new Pete left quickly.
